replacement:
Almost every property has a crowd of ancestors.

Typed questions and bounded answers (P2, P3) are covered four times over.

P(True) gives distributions over labeled options and True/False reformulations (Kadavath et al., [arXiv:2207.05221](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05221)).

Constrained generation bounds any schema by construction (Willard et al., [arXiv:2307.09702](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09702)).

LMQL declares answer kinds up front ([arXiv:2212.06094](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06094)).

LLM2Jev takes choice/noul/score as its three canonical formats ([arXiv:2610.02076](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02076)).

Probabilities by default (P5) are older still.

The Cobbe verifier outputs the probability a solution is correct ([arXiv:2110.14168](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.14168)).

The GenRM direct verifier uses the likelihood of a single 'Yes' token as its score ([arXiv:2408.15240](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15240)).

That last one deserves a pause: option scoring over a two-option slate, trained with the ordinary next-token loss, published in 2024.

If you squint, Jev's choice primitive is GenRM's direct verifier with better marketing and a parallel sampler.

In sum, P2 and P3 are covered four times over, and P5 is older still.
